solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Legal clashes involving having unsuitable actors for set in Macbeth

indicators.note: involving means taking something into the middle, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
letters that clash are jumbled against each other, so the word Legal is rearranged

parts.note: a play with unsuitable actors in its roles is miscast

explanation.surface: A courtroom row over a badly cast production of the Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is not a verb here but a stage setting: the place where part of Shakespeare's play happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare places Duncan's murder at Macbeth's Scottish fortress, so the stronghold is a location of the play.

clue.text: Small boat departs in choppy lagoon

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the jumbled word
choppy water is rough and broken up, so the word lagoon is jumbled

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A little vessel sets off across rough water in a lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppy' rearranges LAGOON into GONOLA, and 'in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian rowing craft, long and narrow, propelled by a single oarsman standing at the stern.

clue.text: Fort in area old king is questing for

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits within the other pieces here

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex, the title of a past King Edward
FT is the abbreviation for fort, as on maps

explanation.surface: A king of old seeks a stronghold in his region.
explanation.definitionFit: Being after something means pursuing or seeking it, as in hunting for treasure.

clue.text: Cross coming between religious fringe groups?

parts.note: inter is the Latin prefix meaning between or among
a sect is a breakaway religious group on the fringe of a faith; the clue's plural loosely describes the type

explanation.surface: An angry remark about something that divides the outer factions of a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for anger; it is the verb meaning to cut across.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cut across one another at a point meet in exactly this way, a verb of crossing.

clue.text: Dimwit's gloom on leaving university

indicators.note: on leaving means when something departs, so a letter drops out of the gloomy word

parts.note: a cloud is a gloomy shadow, as in a cloud hanging over someone

explanation.surface: A slow student falls into a depression after quitting university.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person is called a lump of earth in insulting slang, hence a blockhead.

clue.text: Assistant in penning Aznavour song, say, including piano finish

parts.note: She is a famous 1974 song by the French singer Charles Aznavour

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the abbreviation for say wraps round the next two pieces

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means when introducing an instance
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
to do something in can mean to finish it off, so do means finish

explanation.surface: A helper sings an Aznavour number, ending softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' is not writing but putting animals in a pen, which the farm dog helps with.
explanation.definitionFit: A working dog on a farm helps the shepherd drive flocks into folds and enclosures.

clue.text: Supply mobile home's shell after burning

indicators.note: after tells us the shell comes behind the burning piece

parts.note: something burning is lit, like a fire

indicators.note: a shell is the outside casing, so only the first and last letters of home are used

explanation.surface: Delivering a caravan's burnt-out shell after a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb, but it is the adverb of supple: the definition is 'supply mobile', moving supplely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone supple and agile moves with flexible grace, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Emergency equipment passenger picked up during free journey

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a lift is a free ride in someone's car

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger in a taxi

explanation.surface: A taxi driver collects a passenger while giving someone a free ride.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable boat carried on ships and aircraft for survivors if the vessel sinks.

clue.text: Consider something infuriating when all but first pair flip

indicators.text: when all but first pair flip
indicators.note: everything after the opening two letters is turned round, while those two stay put

parts.note: a red rag to a bull is something that provokes fury

explanation.surface: Thinking about something maddening when all bar two of them turn over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but first pair flip' keeps RE and turns DRAG into GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To look upon or think of someone in a particular way is to view or deem them so.

clue.text: Symbolically write about house, miles away

indicators.note: about means around, so the writing verb surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: to notate is to write music or speech in symbols

explanation.surface: Writing about a house in symbols while far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' sits at the end, looking like part of 'miles away'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not in at their residence is out, absent from their house.

clue.text: Ethnic group's revival set back after expulsion of extremists

indicators.note: extremists are the outermost letters, and expelling them removes the first and last
set back means moved backwards, so the word for revival is read in reverse

parts.note: a revival is a rebirth, as of interest in something

explanation.surface: A people's renaissance suffers a setback once the radicals are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns REBIRTH into HTRIBER; 'after expulsion of extremists' drops its end letters H and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A community linked by shared ancestry, customs and culture is a clan or people.

clue.text: Satyr erroneously holds such a heavenly model the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means backwards, so the concealed letters are read right to left
holds means contains, so the answer sits within the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A mythical goat-man mistakenly holds a celestial model upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds YRERRO within 'Satyr erroneously', and 'the wrong way' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork device showing the planets circling the sun is a model of the heavens.

clue.text: Record time to collect fringe stuff that devalues quickly?

indicators.note: to collect means to gather in, so the record and time take the edge piece between them

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the edge or border of a garment

explanation.surface: A collector's record of time spent gathering marginal items that soon lose value.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-lived items such as tickets and flyers, meant to be thrown away, are collected as transient memorabilia.

clue.text: More mischievous stars who'll often take a bow

definitions.meaning: arch means playfully roguish, and this is its comparative

definitions.text: stars who'll often take a bow
definitions.meaning: Sagittarius, the constellation and zodiac sign, is pictured as a bowman, and the bow is his weapon

explanation.surface: Cheekier stars who frequently bow to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a bow' suggests actors acknowledging applause; here it means picking up a bow to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means slyly playful, so its comparative means slyer; Sagittarius is the bowman constellation.

clue.text: Officer's current answer for drug in settling times

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so the drug letter is swapped out for the other two

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An officer's current answer about drugs during times of settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the E of COLONEL for I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the era when settlers founded overseas territories under imperial rule.

clue.text: Perhaps scrubby site corrupted download

indicators.note: a corrupted computer file has its data scrambled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Perhaps a scrubby website caused a corrupted download.
explanation.walkthrough: 'site' suggests a website alongside 'download', but it means a place covered in scrub or trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Land covered with trees and shrubs, which may include scrubby growth, is a wooded area.

clue.text: Clamorous sound persistently enveloping each swamp

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the sound surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: to ding is to keep ringing or repeating something
a fen is low marshy land

explanation.surface: A noisy ringing goes on and on over each marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise loud enough to make you unable to hear is extremely loud and noisy.

clue.text: Possibly estate's host to miss women's conflict with workers?

indicators.note: a host contains guests, so the car holds the next pieces

parts.note: an estate is a type of car with a large rear load space
a lass is a young miss or girl
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A landed estate hosts a young lady, while women fight with labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxist theory calls the struggle between the working class and capitalists by this name.

clue.text: Undervalue beauty surrounding island races

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the beauty encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the famous motorbike races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A beauty queen on an island underrates the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races held each year on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something seem small or unimportant is to disparage or play it down.

clue.text: Coastal city formerly having fortune run into cove

parts.note: a bomb is a fortune, as in costing a bomb

indicators.note: run into means the two words run together and overlap, sharing the B where they meet

parts.note: a bay is a sheltered inlet or cove

explanation.surface: A city of old where a fortune was sailed into a sheltered inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run into' runs BOMB into BAY so the B ending one starts the other: BOMB and AY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian port now known as Mumbai was officially called by this name until 1995.

clue.text: Continue to need scrubber?

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the continuing word is joined onto the needing one

parts.note: to want is to need, as in the house wants painting
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Keep on wanting something to scrub with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubber' looks like a cleaning tool but is slang for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang for a sexually loose person; the noun use of the adjective meaning immoral.

clue.text: Name not picked up when Queen leaves area near Peckham

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the Queen's letter goes out of the unheard word

parts.note: something not picked up by the ear is unheard
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A name goes unnoticed when the monarch leaves a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Peckham is a district of south London, and the answer is a neighbouring one.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of south-east London in the borough of Southwark, bordering the Peckham neighbourhood.

clue.text: Plain stabs primarily barred in wrestling area

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the wrestling area

parts.note: wrestlers grapple on a mat

indicators.note: barring the first letter means it is shut out of the word

parts.note: to knife someone is to stab them

explanation.surface: Simple stabbing moves are banned in the wrestling ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious and clear to see, as in the evidence was manifest to all.

clue.text: Go for starter of fishcakes to eat in

indicators.note: the starter is the opening, so only the first letter of fishcakes is used

parts.note: acid etches by eating into metal

explanation.surface: Order a fishcake starter to eat in rather than take away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a first course in a restaurant; it gives only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To go and get something and bring it back, as a dog does with a stick.

clue.text: 18 lenses in a special arrangement

indicators.note: a special arrangement means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Belittling lenses placed in a special setup.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' refers to the answer of 18 Across, meaning undervalue; the two can stand in for each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce or diminish something is to make it smaller, as belittling does to its worth.

clue.text: Spelling inaccurate in rant

parts.note: SP is the abbreviation for spelling, as in a proofreader's margin
a guess that is out is wrong or inaccurate

explanation.surface: Bad spelling in a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length in a pompous or emotional way, rather like a declaiming orator.

clue.text: Is going off course a complaint in the Tropics?

definitions.meaning: a ship that ... swings off its heading
a contagious tropical skin infection causing raw sores

explanation.surface: Is drifting off course a disease of hot countries?
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or aircraft that deviates from its heading does this; also a bacterial tropical skin disease.

clue.text: Tailor enjoyed wasting hours with a pint

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the letter for hours is dropped

parts.note: to have had something is to have enjoyed it, as in had a good time

explanation.surface: A tailor wasted hours enjoying a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like the clothier, but it is the verb meaning to modify.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to modify or adjust it to suit particular needs.

clue.text: Humdrum people generally stand to receive instant backing

parts.note: we can mean people in general, as in we all make mistakes

indicators.note: to receive means taking in, so the standing verb holds the next piece

parts.note: to arise is to stand up

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for instant is reversed

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: Dull people tend to stand and receive instant support.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious and tiring, as a dull routine that drains one's interest.

clue.text: Spattering the hogs with dirt's imprudent

indicators.note: spattering scatters things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: dirt's is read as dirt with its s, giving the letters of dirts

explanation.surface: Splashing pigs with mud is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of dirt's counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking foresight figuratively, not considering future consequences; an extended sense of poor distance vision.
